source.title: Lloyd’s Register of Shipping, 1919–20, Volume II—Steamers, with supplements
source.digitization_credit: Lloyd's Register Foundation, Heritage & Education Centre

review.method: OCR located the entries; title page, main entry, supplementary entry, and row crops were then visually inspected. The main entry explicitly points to the same supplementary entry.
review.independent_visual_review: The title page, main entry and supplementary entry were independently visually checked; the names, flags, owner field and explicit cross-reference agree.

review_crop.operation: Rectangular crop only; no resampling or text alteration; retained in research scratch, not repository.

supported_conclusion: The inspected 1919–20 register copy records Sueh under a Turkish flag, corrects its name to Corcovado, and refers to supplementary entry 34203, which lists French Government ownership and a French flag.
limits: This records what the contemporary register and its correction state; it is not a national registration certificate or a prize-court judgment.
The title period and catalogue year do not establish the exact date of transfer, correction, or supplementary publication.
The evidence does not establish the amount paid or completion of the intercepted ten-million proposal, whose currency is unstated.
The main COR section also includes different ships named Corcovado; the Sueh cross-reference, construction and tonnage identify the intended vessel.

review.method: Downloaded the public PDF and XML; parsed the exact case and its parent; visually inspected PDF pages 33 and 34.
